title: Suspension Geometry, Design and Fabrication
author: Erudior
description: Compare five wheel-guidance layouts, springs, dampers and roll control. Design and fabricate a suspension corner, then measure wheel travel, camber and toe. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added two in-depth cases, four assessed questions, two study cards and a practical evidence record. A local motion-ratio measurement and a bump-steer curve with a return check.

lessons.title: Predict wheel motion from link constraints
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Brake, Steering and Suspension Service, Chassis Design, Welding and Fabrication, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

Camber is wheel tilt viewed from the front. Toe describes wheel heading viewed from above. Caster describes the steering axis in side view. Unequal-length links move the top and bottom of the upright on different arcs. The tie rod follows its own arc. If the arcs disagree, wheel heading changes through vertical travel even with the rack held centered. This is bump steer.

## Worked shop case

At reference height toe is +0.10° on a declared toe-in-positive convention. At bump it becomes −0.20°. Subtract the initial reading from the final one. The wheel changed by −0.30°, toward toe-out.

## Guided practice

With toe-in positive, toe moves from +0.2° to −0.1°. Enter the signed change in degrees.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A physical suspension corner, reviewed drawings, measured plots and a revision decision.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Strut, double wishbone, multilink, twist beam and live axle
topics: Strut, double wishbone, multilink, twist beam and live axle
lessons.body:
Identify which features locate the wheel center, carry vertical load and steer the upright. A MacPherson strut provides structural guidance alongside a lower arm; tower height and top mount matter. Double wishbones use upper and lower arms, allowing the designer to tune camber change through hard-point placement, with extra packaging and joints. A multilink system distributes constraints across links and bushings; changing one pickup can alter toe, camber and compliance together. Count and function of constraints matter more than marketing names.

A twist-beam rear uses trailing arms joined by a beam that resists relative twist, so left and right motion is coupled. A live axle carries the differential and axle shafts with the wheels and generally adds unsprung mass. Independent drives can mount the differential to the chassis and use articulated shafts. Compare wheel travel, camber and toe, roll behavior, steering clearance, joint articulation, drive/brake loads and the routes those loads take to the body.

## Worked shop case

A short strut tower conflicts with an intended hood line. A double-wishbone concept offers a different upper load path but needs space for the upper arm through bump and steer. Before changing the chassis, overlay wheel, tire, arms and spring/damper across travel and identify pickup reactions on both candidate frames.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A beam axle model moves one wheel upward while the other rests on the ground. What do you watch?
step: Observe axle orientation and motion of the far wheel and body.
step: Compare this with independent wheel guidance at the same body position.
answer: Record coupled movement and contact/clearance effects under the same boundary conditions.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Build the course's original suspension corner. Draw a second architecture for the same upright and compare hard points, body load paths, wheel/toe/camber travel and service access. Record which actual measurements validate your final layout.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Springs, dampers, anti-roll bars and compliant joints
topics: Springs, dampers, anti-roll bars and compliant joints
lessons.body:
Coil springs support load by deflecting. A leaf pack can support load and help locate an axle. A torsion bar supplies spring force through twist. An air spring uses compressed gas and its effective area and installed volume influence rate. A damper dissipates motion energy; a conventional damper cannot replace the spring's static support function. An anti-roll bar couples left/right motion and adds resistance to difference in wheel travel. Matched heave on an ideal symmetric installation produces little bar twist. A strut can combine spring support, damping and wheel guidance.

Define motion ratio as spring travel divided by wheel travel near the position of interest. Over a small interval of nearly constant motion ratio, neglect geometric stiffness from spring preload. In this ideal model the wheel rate due to the spring is spring rate times motion ratio squared. Do not use an inverse definition in the same calculation. Bushing stiffness, tire compliance, geometry and anti-roll elements affect real corner response. Inspect clearance, joint misalignment, droop stops, bump stops and spring containment through travel using the approved unloaded fixture. Stored spring energy calls for the correct equipment and supervision.

## Worked shop case

A 40 N/mm spring moves 0.75 mm for 1 mm of wheel travel. Its local wheel rate is 40 × 0.75² = 22.5 N/mm. Moving the spring pickup inward can reduce that rate even with exactly the same spring. It can also change damper shaft speed for a given wheel speed.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: Select between two dampers with similar length but different compression curves.
step: Identify wheel-speed range and motion ratio.
step: Convert to damper shaft speed and compare the supplied force curves.
answer: Check travel and hard limits separately. Length alone cannot establish damping performance.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Measure wheel travel and spring or damper pickup travel at three rig positions. Compare the local motion ratios with the drawing and document bump, droop, containment and reviewer disposition before considering a vehicle installation.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Lay out and review the hard points
lessons.body:
Set chassis-fixed datums, signs and a nominal ride height. Locate control-arm pivots, ball joints, steering rack and tie-rod ends in three dimensions. Include the chosen upright, tire envelope, damper and brake-hose routing. Predict camber and toe at several fixed travel stations, including droop. Assess combined braking, bump and cornering loads with a qualified chassis reviewer before any vehicle-use arm is made.

## Worked shop case

Using shock travel divided by wheel travel as the motion ratio, 15 mm shock movement for 30 mm wheel movement gives 0.5. Reversing this ratio changes the predicted wheel rate, so explicitly state which displacement is the numerator.

## Guided practice

A damper moves 18 mm during 30 mm of wheel travel. Using damper/wheel convention, what is the motion ratio?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

Select a real upright and wheel. Submit a dimensioned coordinate table, damper/wheel convention, travel stations and predicted toe/camber curves. Mark load cases, joint-angle limits and clearance envelopes. Have a qualified chassis reviewer evaluate the proposed joints, materials and structure before vehicle-use fabrication.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Turn spring position into wheel rate and travel margin
topics: Turn spring position into wheel rate and travel margin
lessons.body:
Define motion ratio before using it. In this lesson r means spring displacement divided by vertical wheel displacement near one ride position. For an ideal lossless linear mechanism, force balance and displacement give wheel rate approximately equal to spring rate times r squared. A coilover moved inward on a control arm can lower wheel rate even if it retains the same spring. A real ratio can change through travel and with link angle.

**Worked comparison.** A 60 N/mm spring with r = 0.80 gives 38.4 N/mm at the wheel. Moving the pickup so r = 0.60 yields 21.6 N/mm at the same local condition. A 40 mm wheel displacement corresponds to 24 mm at the spring if the latter ratio stays constant. Check damper stroke, spring seating, bump-stop engagement, tire clearance, hose routing and joint articulation across travel. Rate at ride height does not prove that travel is safe at bump and droop.

**Plan a measurement.** On the unloaded geometry fixture choose a repeatable wheel-center datum, zero position and a dummy spring-length gauge. Mark independent wheel and spring scales. Make a prediction at three positions. Compare a strut, double wishbone and linked solid axle by locating the spring and the wheel-force path. Keep actual spring removal and structural pickup design within appropriately equipped and qualified work.

lessons.title: Build an unloaded front corner fixture
lessons.body:
Fabricate locating fixtures and the instructional arm or link to the reviewed drawing. Use suitable commercially specified bearings, ball joints, hub and fasteners. Isolate the rig from vehicle use and spring preload during the geometry survey. Secure the upright and any moving masses so they cannot fall. Observe joint articulation and hose and tire envelopes while an operator moves the rig through its permitted travel.

## Worked shop case

The drawing predicts 5 mm clearance at bump. A witness strip is crushed during the sweep. The nominal drawing has failed to describe the as-built envelope. Identify the interference and revise the assembly before accepting that position.

## Guided practice

Predicted clearance is 8 mm and measured clearance is 3 mm. Give the magnitude of the discrepancy in mm.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

A spring-free geometry sweep demonstrates kinematics. Safe road use also requires material, joint, fatigue, steering and vehicle-level review under the intended-use criteria. Use guarding and energy controls where applicable in the workplace and check the rules in the registration jurisdiction. Preserve an inspection record for safety-related equipment. A supplier's certification for an item covers that item; it does not certify the assembled car.

[OSHA — control of hazardous energy, 29 CFR 1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147) · [OSHA — machine guarding, 29 CFR 1910.212](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212) · [NHTSA — equipment standards and a specific kit-manufacturer interpretation](https://www.nhtsa.gov/interpretations/19664ztv) · [Colorado DMV — certified VIN inspections for custom-built vehicles](https://dmv.colorado.gov/vin-inspections)

## Workshop preparation

Support moving masses independently, guard pinch points and use an experienced fabrication supervisor. Remove spring loads by an appropriate professional procedure before this unloaded test. Mark the fixture as a prototype.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: Separate spring rate from installed wheel rate
topics: Separate spring rate from installed wheel rate
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Wheel guidance and compliance, Suspension service hardware. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Matched springs, dampers or coilovers
- Anti-roll bar and end links
- Alignment and adjustable arms
- Ride-height lift or larger tire package
- Bushings or spherical joints

## Worked example

A spring-free teaching corner moves the spring seat 20 mm while the wheel moves 40 mm. Here the local spring/wheel motion ratio is 0.5. With a 60 N/mm spring, near-constant ratio and negligible preload geometry effects, local spring contribution to wheel rate is 15 N/mm. A shorter spring by itself says nothing about that rate.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: If the same 60 N/mm spring has a local spring/wheel ratio of 0.8, what rate follows in the same model?
step: Multiply 60 by 0.8 squared.
answer: 38.4 N/mm. Recheck wheel travel, bump-stop contact and damping separately.
```

## Independent workshop

Use the spring-free rig to compare two pickup or ride-height configurations. Record wheel position, motion ratio, toe, camber and clearance over actual travel.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Measure bump steer separately from lateral wheel movement
topics: Measure bump steer separately from lateral wheel movement
lessons.body:
A tie rod tracing a different arc from the suspension links can steer the upright while the steering rack stays fixed. Measuring the lateral motion of one rim point alone mixes steer with the entire wheel moving sideways. Use two points separated fore and aft on a rigid toe plate, measured from a common fixture reference. State which direction is positive before taking data. An actual alignment rig needs its own calibrated procedure.

**Worked fixture.** Two gauge points are 400 mm apart. Through one travel step the front point moves laterally +3 mm and the rear moves +1 mm relative to the baseline. Their mean, +2 mm, represents the plate's lateral translation near its center. Their 2 mm differential over 400 mm gives a small yaw change of roughly 0.005 rad, or 0.29 degrees. The toe-in or toe-out label depends on side of the vehicle and the sign convention. Reversing the two gauge labels reverses the computed sign.

**Independent work.** On a spring-free, securely supported hand-operated trainer, lock the rack reference and measure front and rear gauge points at bump, ride and droop. Take a return-travel reading to reveal play or fixture movement. Plot differential displacement against wheel travel. Test a reviewed reversible change on the unloaded trainer and repeat the same sweep. Submit both curves and state the limitations before any vehicle application.

```assignment
lab: case-record
```

lessons.title: Plot the measured curve and evaluate a revision
lessons.body:
Plot wheel travel on the horizontal axis and individual toe and camber readings on separate vertical axes. Repeat the midpoint on the return sweep to expose play or hysteresis. Change one mount location only under a reviewed fixture revision. A successful kinematic sweep does not demonstrate weld strength, fatigue life, high-speed stability or crash protection.

## Worked shop case

Two curves agree at ride height but diverge at bump. Compare the full curves and physical clearance. A revised tie-rod height can improve the bump end and worsen droop, so inspect both.

## Guided practice

The same travel station reads +0.4° on the upward sweep and +0.1° on return. What is their absolute difference in degrees?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

Two measured sweeps, predicted curves and a justified revision are present; structural review remains separately documented. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Wheel guidance; Spring and damper; Roll control and travel limits; Joints, knuckle and control arms. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wheel guidance | Strut / double wishbone / multilink / twist beam / live axle | Guidance constraints, cross-axle coupling and body loads differ. | Plot camber and toe against wheel position using consistent datums. |
| Spring and damper | Coil / leaf / torsion / air; separate shock / structural strut | Static load support, damping and wheel location are distinct functions. | Measure local motion ratio, wheel rate estimate and available stroke. |
| Roll control and travel limits | Anti-roll bar / no cross-link; bump / droop stops | Cross-axle twist and terminal travel limits address different modes. | Check opposite-wheel travel, travel extremes and spring containment on the approved rig. |
| Joints, knuckle and control arms | Ball joint / compliant bushing / spherical bearing | Articulation, stiffness, contamination, fatigue and service life change with choice. | Check misalignment, binding, loads and service limits against the reviewed design. |

references.title: Wheel guidance and compliance · Upright or steering knuckle to Coil spring
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Upright or steering knuckle

**Function.** Connects wheel bearing, steering arm and suspension points.

**Design.** Review loads, bearing fit, steering geometry, brake attachment and fatigue.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Choose compatible rated upright or have original design independently engineered and manufactured.

**Verify.** Verify bore, pickup coordinates, cracks and interfaces using reviewed criteria.

### Upper control arm

**Function.** Locates upper upright and sets geometry through travel.

**Design.** Define hard points, loads, bushings, articulation and clearance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fixture a teaching arm to reviewed drawing; qualify structural joints separately.

**Verify.** Measure pickup centers and camber/toe over rig travel.

### Lower control arm

**Function.** Transfers wheel forces to lower chassis pickups.

**Design.** Determine bending and axial loads, motion ratio and ball-joint geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use traceable arm or reviewed fabrication fixture and joining method.

**Verify.** Check travel limits, fit, fastener retention and inspection evidence.

### Trailing arm

**Function.** Locates wheel longitudinally while swinging about a pivot.

**Design.** Choose pivot axis, compliance, axle clearance and load path.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched donor part or engineer and jig prototype before production.

**Verify.** Measure wheel path and compliance clearance.

### Toe link

**Function.** Controls rear or auxiliary steering angle through travel.

**Design.** Choose inner/outer pivot positions, adjuster range and locking method.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched ends and spacers with documented engagement and articulation.

**Verify.** Plot toe over travel and lock measured adjustment.

### Ball joint

**Function.** Provides multi-axis connection for loaded suspension members.

**Design.** Match taper, load direction, retention and articulation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install a rated joint with exact press or bolt-on procedure.

**Verify.** Check seating, retention, movement and play limits.

### Control-arm bushing

**Function.** Allows controlled motion and isolates vibration.

**Design.** Choose rubber, elastomer or spherical joint for load and compliance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Press the specified orientation; tighten bonded bushes at prescribed position.

**Verify.** Record ride-height condition and verify free travel.

### Coil spring

**Function.** Carries load elastically.

**Design.** Match rate, installed length, allowable travel and seat geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Source rated spring and fit with approved stored-energy controls.

**Verify.** Check ride height, containment and full travel.

references.title: Wheel guidance and compliance · Leaf spring to Droop limiter
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Leaf spring

**Function.** Supports load and may locate a rigid axle.

**Design.** Choose pack rate, camber, shackle path and axle attachment.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install rated matched pack with specified bolts and U-bolts.

**Verify.** Check axle alignment, shackle clearance and required torque follow-up.

### Air spring

**Function.** Supports load using compressed gas.

**Design.** Determine pressure range, effective area, minimum height and stops.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched air spring and rated fittings on reviewed mounts.

**Verify.** Check leaks, alignment and clearance throughout travel.

### Damper

**Function.** Dissipates motion energy.

**Design.** Choose stroke, extended length, motion ratio and damping curves.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install rated unit with proper bushings, orientation and hardware.

**Verify.** Measure bump/droop margin and inspect response and leaks.

### Strut and top mount

**Function.** Guide the wheel and transmit spring/damper loads to the tower.

**Design.** Match knuckle interface, tower load, bearing and travel.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a matched strut assembly and approved spring-handling procedure.

**Verify.** Check bearing rotation, wheel alignment and full steer clearance.

### Anti-roll bar

**Function.** Adds roll stiffness through opposed wheel movement.

**Design.** Choose torsional stiffness, lever arms, mounting and balance.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit a reviewed bar, lubricated bushes as specified and correctly oriented arms.

**Verify.** Verify through-travel clearance and neutral setup at stated load.

### End link

**Function.** Transfers suspension motion to the bar.

**Design.** Choose length, load rating and joint articulation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched joints and establish specified preload or neutral setting.

**Verify.** Check for binding and record ride-height setup.

### Bump stop

**Function.** Limits jounce and progressively transfers load.

**Design.** Define engagement point, energy absorption and protected clearances.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install rated stop and reviewed support pad on intended contact path.

**Verify.** Measure contact position and remaining clearance.

### Droop limiter

**Function.** Restricts extension before joints or shafts overtravel.

**Design.** Choose load rating, length and anchor geometry.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the designed limiting device to reviewed anchors.

**Verify.** Check limiting sequence and joint angles at full extension.

### Solid axle housing

**Function.** Carries differential, wheel ends and link reactions.

**Design.** Match track, axle loads, bracket geometry and lubrication attitude.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Select inspected housing; qualified shop fixtures any structural modification.

**Verify.** Measure straightness, mount positions and drive angles.

### Panhard rod or lateral locator

**Function.** Controls lateral motion of a linked axle.

**Design.** Choose length, inclination, roll center and end-joint travel.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit reviewed rod and brackets at design ride height.

**Verify.** Measure axle side shift and clearance through travel.

### Spring perch and isolator

**Function.** Locate the spring and isolate contact noise.

**Design.** Match coil end shape, contact area, retention and allowable travel.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Seat the correct isolator and index the coil to its specified stop.

**Verify.** Verify position at ride height and full droop.

### Strut bearing

**Function.** Allows spring/strut assembly to turn during steering.

**Design.** Match axial load, bearing stack and orientation.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched bearing and spring-seat order with approved spring controls.

**Verify.** Check smooth rotation and absence of spring wind-up or binding.

### Damper dust boot

**Function.** Protects piston rod and seal from contamination.

**Design.** Match rod, travel and space around the bump stop.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit compatible boot without trapping or limiting moving components.

**Verify.** Inspect through stroke for rubbing, tears or detachment.

### Leaf-spring shackle

**Function.** Accommodates eye-to-eye length change as a spring flexes.

**Design.** Define shackle angle, travel, loads and clearance to body.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched pins and bushes to the specified loaded-state sequence.

**Verify.** Check for inversion, bind and body contact across travel.

### Axle U-bolt and seat

**Function.** Clamp a leaf-sprung axle to its locating seat.

**Design.** Match axle diameter, material, clamp, thread and locking method.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit specified new hardware where required and tighten evenly to source sequence.

**Verify.** Record seating, axle position and required torque reinspection.

references.body:
**Purpose.** Change ride height, wheel rate or damping response for a stated use.

**Design and baseline.** Measure axle loads, motion ratio, ride height and existing bump/droop travel. Choose rate, damping curve, stroke and spring retention together.

**Build and installation.** Mock wheel travel on the spring-free approved corner rig. Fit rated matched assemblies using approved stored-energy controls, set initial height by product data, then settle and align.

**Test and disposition.** Record bump/droop, tire and shaft clearance, camber/toe curves and repeatable ride/handling behavior. Reject bottoming, unseated springs or joint bind.

**Design and baseline.** Map lowest body, axle and differential points separately. Check caster, driveshaft and CV angles, hose length, wheel travel, rollover/stability effects, calibration triggers and local equipment-height requirements.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

writing.title: Design the first suspension corner
writing.prompt: Select a real upright and wheel. Submit a dimensioned coordinate table, damper/wheel convention, travel stations and predicted toe/camber curves. Mark load cases, joint-angle limits and clearance envelopes. Have a qualified chassis reviewer evaluate the proposed joints, materials and structure before vehicle-use fabrication. Include a labeled drawing or table in the work record and identify the applicable shop or legal requirement.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Wheel guidance; Spring and damper; Roll control and travel limits; Joints, knuckle and control arms. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. Identify a real model or part number for each shortlisted candidate. Compare a sourced limit or performance figure under common conditions, interfaces, legal or shop implications and service access. Defend your choice and explain one change that would reverse it. Link your drawing and physical observation or measurement to the build record.

writing.title: Workshop record · Separate spring rate from installed wheel rate
writing.prompt: Use the spring-free rig to compare two pickup or ride-height configurations. Record wheel position, motion ratio, toe, camber and clearance over actual travel. List your donor or drawing revision, part identities, position, material or rating, method, who made or fitted each item, and the governing source. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement. An inert prototype or mock-up qualifies for this comparison exercise when the vehicle modification requires specialist or legal approval. Identify exactly which vehicle results are still unproven.
